subject: Request: Headroom variance for dedicated GPU pool (Zenith Corp)
messages:
From: Alexandra Park <alex.park@zenithcorp.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@zenithcorp.com, Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@zenithcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for temporary headroom variance on Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the discussion last week. We hit our seasonal forecast and expect a planned burst for a multi-day marketing personalization push (Mar 22-25). Our Reserved GPU commitment under ZEN-2027-043 covers a steady baseline, but we need a formal exception to the "headroom"/burst policy so that spikes up to ~2.5x baseline for short windows won't trigger queueing that violates our internal SLAs.

Specifically we are asking for: 
- A documented variance to allow scheduled headroom of +150% for up to 48 hours per quarter without queue-based throttling credits or re-routing.
- A temporary guaranteed throughput floor of 90% of baseline during the window (to avoid throttled tail latency impacting customer flows).
- A brief addendum to the Dedicated SLA and confirmation of metric collection that would be available to our SREs (token-level latency + queue-depth).

I've attached a two-page summary and sample metrics from last year's run. Can you route to the right person to evaluate? We prefer an answer within 72 hours if possible — this will determine our campaign go/no-go.

Cheers,
Alexandra Park
Head of Infrastructure Ops
Zenith Corp

Attachments: zenith-proposed-addendum.pdf (PDF), sample-metrics-03-01.csv (CSV)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Park <alex.park@zenithcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for temporary headroom variance on Dedicated GPU pool

Alexandra — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, much appreciated. Looping in Marissa (Dedicated runtime lead) and Karthik (Enterprise sales/contracting) to evaluate the operational and contractual implications.

Quick response while they dig in:
- We can support scheduled headroom but it requires an SLA addendum that clarifies how preemption and fallback routing behave during the allowance window.
- We will instrument per-token latency and queueing metrics and can expose a read-only dashboard/metric stream to your SREs during the window; Marissa will confirm exact metrics and retention.
- Pricing for guaranteed throughput during a variance typically follows a short-term reservation uplift — Karthik will propose options (crediting vs temporary commit).

We'll aim to respond with a concrete proposal within 48 hours. If you need signoff faster, tell us which internal approver at Zenith needs to be copied.

Regards,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Alexandra / Lukas —

Thanks for the details. Technical notes from runtime perspective: 
- We can create a scheduled "headroom window" tied to the dedicated pool that relaxes the default queueing backpressure for up to 72 hours per quarter. During the window we would:
  * Allow short-term batching windows to grow (reduces immediate throttling)
  * Reserve a small percentage of the pool as a non-preemptible lane for your critical routes to maintain 90% baseline throughput.
- Trade-offs: tail latency risk increases at very high concurrency; we recommend you pin mission-critical routes to the non-preemptible lane.
- Observability: we'll push a dedicated snapshots feed (per-route p50/p95/p99, queue-depth, tokens/sec) and provide a shared dashboard link.

I attached a diagram that shows the proposed traffic carve-out and metric names. If Zenith can commit to an uplift for the pilot window (either credit draw or a short-term commit) we can guarantee the carve-out. Proposed docs attached: sla-coverage-diagram.png.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Dedicated Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-coverage-diagram.png (PNG)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Park <alex.park@zenithcorp.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for temporary headroom variance on Dedicated GPU pool

Alexandra — quick commercial proposal for the short pilot: 
- Option A (crediting): Grant Zenith a one-off credit equal to 40% of the expected incremental usage during the window; Redwood keeps the headroom carve-out but charges overage at standard reserved rates.
- Option B (short commit): Temporary commit for the 48-hour window at 1.5x baseline at a 20% uplift to your monthly reserved rate for that billing month. This guarantees the non-preemptible lane and the throughput floor.

Operationally, we need:
1) Signed SLA addendum specifying the carve-out and fallback (we can draft).
2) A scheduled activation window (start/end UTC).
3) Primary contact for operational handoff (SRE pager or runbook link).

If you are comfortable with Option B we can put the addendum into DocuSign today and lock the allocations. I've also attached an internal example of how the uplift would amortize into monthly spend for visibility.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: zenith-cost-example.xlsx (XLSX) (sent internally, not attached to external mail)

We reviewed Option B internally and prefer the temporary commit route for predictability. We need the guaranteed non-preemptible lane for the following routes: /personalization/serve and /campaign/render. Proposed activation: 2027-03-22T00:00:00Z to 2027-03-24T23:59:00Z (48 hours).

Procurement asks that the addendum include: clear metric definitions for breach, a runbook for on-call escalation, and evidence of metric retention for 90 days. We are ready to sign once those are included. Please send the DocuSign link.
